### Annual billing
An annual plan costs the same as 10 months of monthly billing. It renews automatically on the anniversary of the purchase date, and the Owner receives a reminder email 14 days before each renewal. {"reply": "Downgrading to Basic
When would the downgrade take effect?

1. The downgrade takes effect at the start of the next billing period, so you keep Pro features until then.
2. On an annual plan, a downgrade takes effect when the annual period ends.
3. There is no refund for the rest of the current period.

4. Before you can downgrade to Basic, the organization has to fit within its limits:

1. Archive projects until no more than 3 are active.
2. Remove or suspend members until no more than 5 remain, including pending invitations.
3. Remove guests from any project that has more than 10.
4. Delete files until storage is under 10 GB. Files larger than 100 MB that are already stored are kept, but new uploads must be under 100 MB.
5. Turn off single sign-on, SCIM, and the IP allowlist. The audit log is kept, but it stops recording new events and becomes visible again only if you upgrade.

5. The Change plan page checks each of these and lists anything that still needs to be done.

# Administrator Guide
## 1. Organization settings
### 1.1 Name and address
The organization name appears in the sidebar, in invitation emails, and on invoices. Change it under Settings > Organization > General. # Administrator Guide
## 7. Security settings
### 7.3 IP allowlist
On the Pro plan, Admins can limit sign-ins and API requests to a list of IP address ranges, under Settings > Security > IP allowlist. Enter up to 50 ranges in CIDR notation, such as 203.0.113.0/24. Requests from other addresses are refused with an error that names the allowlist. The Owner is exempt from the allowlist, so a wrong entry can't lock everyone out. Webhook deliveries are not affected, because they go from our servers to yours.

# API Reference
## Versioning and deprecation
The version is part of the path. Changes that could break existing clients, such as removing a field or changing its type, are made only in a new version. Adding fields, endpoints, or event types isn't considered breaking, so clients should ignore fields they don't know.
When an endpoint or version is deprecated, its responses include a Deprecation header, and a Sunset header with the date it will stop working. A deprecated version keeps working for at least 6 months after the announcement.
